1.title: Asset Protection: Lifecycle, Configuration and Change Management
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Asset Protection: Lifecycle, Configuration and Change Management. It covers the exam area five. Security Operations and Incident Response. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. five point four Understand asset protection: Asset lifecycle management (for example End Of Life (E O L) software and devices). Configuration and change management. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five. Security Operations and Incident Response (seventeen point three percent). Exam format: an adaptive exam of one hundred to one hundred twenty-five questions in two hours; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official I S C two C C exam outline.

1.title: Asset management
1.text: Asset management. You cannot protect what you do not know you have. An asset inventory lists hardware, software, data, cloud services and A I models, each with an owner, location and classification. Hardware. Laptops, servers, network devices, I O T devices. Software. Operating systems, applications, licenses. Data. Databases, documents, A I training sets. Services. Cloud accounts, A I services and bots. Exam tip: Inventory first. Unknown or shadow assets are never patched or monitored.

1.title: The asset life cycle
1.text: The asset life cycle. The figure shows this: The asset life cycle from acquisition to disposal.

1.title: The asset life cycle, continued
1.text: The asset life cycle. Acquire. Check the vendor, requirements, secure by design. Deploy. Harden, baseline configuration, record in the inventory. Operate and maintain. Patch, monitor, back up, review access. Retire and dispose. Remove from the network, sanitize data, recycle or destroy, update inventory. End of life (E O L) or end of support (E O S) means the vendor no longer provides security updates. E O L assets are high risk. Replace or upgrade. Best answer. Compensating controls. Isolate, restrict access, monitor when replacement is not yet possible. Plan ahead. Track support dates in the inventory. Exam tip: E O L means no more patches. The best fix is to replace; isolation is only a stopgap.

1.title: Configuration management
1.text: Configuration management. Configuration management keeps systems in a known, approved, secure state. Baseline. The approved secure configuration of a type of system. Hardening. Removing unneeded services, accounts and software, changing defaults, closing ports. Configuration item. Any component under control (a server, a setting). Configuration management database (C M D B). Stores configuration items and their relationships. Drift. Changes away from the baseline; detect and correct them.

1.title: Change management
1.text: Change management. Change management makes sure changes are requested, reviewed, approved, tested and recorded, so they do not break security or availability. one Request. Describe the change and the reason. two Assess. Review impact and risk, including security. three Approve. A change advisory board (C A B) or manager approves. four Test. Try it in a test environment. five Implement. Carry it out in a planned window with a rollback plan. six Review and document. Verify success, update records and the baseline. Emergency changes are faster but still recorded and reviewed afterwards. Patch management is change management for updates: find, test, deploy, verify. Critical vulnerabilities are patched first. Exam tip: No change without approval, testing and a rollback plan. Unauthorized changes break the baseline and are a risk.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. What should be done first to protect all of the assets of an organization? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Create and maintain an asset inventory. You cannot protect what you do not know you have, so an inventory comes first.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An old server runs software that the vendor no longer supports with security updates. What is the best long-term action? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Replace or upgrade the unsupported software. End-of-life software gets no patches, so replacement is the best answer; isolation is only temporary.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A retired laptop with customer data is given to charity. What must be done first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Sanitize the storage so data cannot be recovered. Data must be sanitized at disposal, and deleting files is not enough.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which term describes the approved secure configuration used as the standard for a type of system? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A baseline. A baseline is the approved secure configuration; drift is a deviation from it.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A developer wants to change a firewall rule in production right away. What does change management require? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Request, assess, approve, test and record the change. Changes follow a controlled process: request, assessment, approval, testing, implementation and documentation.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which plan element lets a team undo a failed change? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A rollback plan. A rollback plan describes how to return to the previous state.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does E O L mean for a product? Answer: The vendor no longer provides security updates. Question two. What is a baseline? Answer: The approved secure configuration. Question three. What is configuration drift? Answer: Changes away from the baseline.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does a C A B do? Answer: Reviews and approves changes. Question five. What is hardening? Answer: Removing unneeded services and changing defaults. Question six. What are the asset life cycle stages? Answer: Acquire, deploy, operate and maintain, retire and dispose.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Inventory: know what you have; owner, location, classification. Life cycle: acquire, deploy, operate and maintain, retire and dispose (sanitize). E O L: no patches; replace; isolate as a stopgap. Configuration: baseline, hardening, C M D B, detect drift. Change: request, assess, approve (C A B), test, implement with rollback, review.
